name: Roll call
chair_script: Good morning, delegates, and welcome to the {committee}. The chair will now call the roll. When you hear your delegation's name, raise your placard and answer "present" or "present and voting". A delegation that is present and voting may not abstain on substantive votes.
chair_next: Call each delegation, or let students answer on their devices. Delegations with no student are answered by the engine and marked computed. When the roll is complete, announce how many are present and the majority needed, then move to setting the agenda.
student_prompt: Answer the roll for your delegation: Present, or Present and voting. If you choose Present and voting you can't abstain on the resolution.

name: Setting the agenda
chair_script: With {present} delegations present, a simple majority is {majority}. The floor is open for a motion to set the agenda. Is there a motion to set the agenda to {agenda}? Is there a second? Are there any objections? Seeing none, the agenda is set.
chair_next: Type the agenda topic. With one topic, set it by consent; with two, take a motion and vote. Then open the general speakers list.
student_prompt: Listen for the motion to set the agenda. You can second it, or ask to speak for or against it.

name: Opening speeches
chair_script: The chair now opens the general speakers list on {agenda}. Delegates wishing to be added, please raise your placards. Speaking time is {speaking_time} seconds. Delegates who finish early may yield their remaining time to the chair, to questions, or to another delegate.
chair_next: Add delegations to the speakers list (students can add themselves), start each speaker's timer, and handle yields. When most delegations have spoken, ask for points or motions.
student_prompt: Add yourself to the speakers list and give your opening speech: your country's position on {agenda} and what you want the resolution to say.

name: Moderated and unmoderated caucus
chair_script: Are there any points or motions on the floor? The chair has received a motion for a moderated caucus of {minutes} minutes with {seconds} seconds speaking time on the topic of {topic}. Is there a second? We will now vote on this motion. All those in favour? All those against? The motion passes.
chair_next: Take motions in order of precedence: the most disruptive first. A moderated caucus has its own speakers list; an unmoderated caucus is free lobbying and drafting time. When a draft resolution has enough sponsors, move to introducing it.
student_prompt: Propose or second a motion for a caucus. In an unmoderated caucus, lobby other delegations and work on the draft resolution with your bloc.

name: Draft resolution introduced
chair_script: The chair has received a draft resolution on {agenda} with the required number of sponsors. Would the sponsors please come forward and read the operative clauses? The chair will then take a short round of questions.
chair_next: Open the resolution workspace on the projector. Sponsors read the operative clauses; take questions to the sponsors. Then open the floor to amendments.
student_prompt: Sponsors: read your operative clauses. Everyone else: read the draft in the workspace and decide which paragraphs you would change.

name: Amendments
chair_script: The floor is open for amendments. A friendly amendment, agreed by all sponsors, is added without a vote. An unfriendly amendment needs a seconder and will be voted on before the resolution. The chair recognises the delegate of …
chair_next: In the workspace, mark amendments friendly, or table them for a vote. Before each vote you can run a whip count so students predict how named delegations will vote.
student_prompt: Propose an amendment to a paragraph in the workspace, find a seconder, and lobby for it. Support or oppose other amendments.

name: Into voting procedure
chair_script: We are now entering voting procedure. The doors are closed: no one may enter or leave the room, and there is no talking or passing of notes. Delegates may raise only points of order. We will vote first on the unfriendly amendments, in the order they were submitted, and then on the resolution as a whole.
chair_next: Start the whip count (students predict how named delegations will vote), give them a minute, then open the division. Predictions lock when voting opens.
student_prompt: No talking. If the chair has started a whip count, predict how your named delegations will vote before voting opens.

name: Division
chair_script: We will now vote on {target}. A simple majority of those present and voting is required. All those in favour, please raise your placards. All those against. All those abstaining. The chair will now announce the result.
chair_next: Open the vote. Students vote on their devices; delegations without a student vote automatically and are labelled computed. Close the vote to announce the result, then go to the debrief.
student_prompt: Vote for your delegation: Yes, No or Abstain (you can't abstain if you answered Present and voting).

name: Results and debrief
chair_script: With {yes} in favour, {no} against and {abstain} abstentions, the {target_short} {result}. The chair thanks all delegates. Let's look at how well we read the room.
chair_next: Show the debrief: each student's whip accuracy against the votes actually cast, how the prediction engine did on this vote, and which delegations decided the result.
student_prompt: Read your debrief: how many delegations you predicted correctly, which votes decided the result, and how your own vote matched your country's mandate.
